overview.text: California’s gold story includes placer deposits, hard-rock mining, and the rush triggered by the 1848 discovery at Sutter’s sawmill. The California Geological Survey’s historical account also describes discoveries before 1848; the rush date is not the state’s first discovery date.

facts.label: Historic gold sites mapped
facts.definition: Sites on CGS Gold Districts of California map MM009. This is a historical map inventory, not a count of active mines.

history.title: The discovery that sparked the rush
history.text: CGS dates James Marshall’s discovery at Sutter’s sawmill on the South Fork of the American River to January 24, 1848. Treat that landmark separately from earlier discoveries.

places.title: South Fork of the American River
places.text: The river associated with Marshall’s 1848 discovery, according to CGS. This historical connection does not establish a present-day place to pan.

destinations.title: Marshall Gold Discovery · designated river panning
destinations.text: Try hand panning in the park’s designated river area in Coloma. Ask staff to identify the permitted reach of the South Fork of the American River. The paid trough lesson is a separate option.

tripFacts.text: 310 Back Street, Coloma, CA 95613. Gold Discovery Museum: 530-622-3470.
River panning is permitted in a designated area during park hours. Ask a park employee where to pan; this permission does not cover the entire river.
The 2017 park brochure specifies hands and pan only. Its map labels the recreational panning area. Confirm the current boundary and equipment limits with staff.
tripFacts.locator: PDF p. 6: Please Remember; p. 7: map

tripFacts.text: Published vehicle day use is $10. The optional trough lesson is $12 per person; it is separate from river panning. Check current charges before travel.
tripFacts.locator: Operating Hours and Fees; Gold Panning lessons

tripFacts.text: Day-use hours vary by season. The park page currently gives differing closing times in its header and seasonal schedule, so confirm today’s hours. Closed Thanksgiving and Christmas; lessons may be canceled by weather or heat.
tripFacts.locator: Park Hours; Operating Hours; program conditions

tripFacts.text: Museum, picnic areas, restrooms, drinking water and parking. Ask staff about the river approach and mobility needs; park amenities do not establish an accessible riverbank.

beforeYouGo: Ask staff for the designated panning reach before taking equipment to the river.
Check current river conditions and opening hours; a historical map is not a live access report.
Confirm lesson availability if you want instruction rather than independent river panning.

overview.text: North Carolina’s Reed Gold Mine history begins with Conrad Reed’s 1799 find in Little Meadow Creek. The official account describes the growth of early mining and the work of enslaved people, whose contributions belong in the story alongside mine owners.

facts.label: First documented discovery
facts.definition: Reed Gold Mine is identified by North Carolina Historic Sites as the first documented gold find in the United States; the find was in Cabarrus County.

history.title: Remembering Peter’s contribution
history.text: North Carolina Historic Sites identifies Peter, an enslaved boy, as the finder of a large nugget during the first year of John Reed’s 1803 mining partnership. The account also records that the partnership supplied enslaved labor.

places.title: Little Meadow Creek · Cabarrus County
places.text: The official Reed Gold Mine history locates Conrad Reed’s 1799 discovery here. It is a historical reference, not an open-access prospecting recommendation.

destinations.title: Reed Gold Mine · learn at the troughs
destinations.text: A supervised panning experience at the historic site near Midland. Practice at the site’s troughs with instructor help; this program does not grant access to pan in Little Meadow Creek.

tripFacts.text: 9621 Reed Mine Road, Midland, NC 28107. Call 704-721-4653.
Buy panning tickets at the gift-shop counter, first come, first served. Advance booking is not offered for individual panning sessions.
Use the managed trough program and follow instructor guidance. Children under eight can help an adult but cannot have their own pan.
tripFacts.locator: Gold Panning: instruction and age limits

tripFacts.text: Panning is $5 plus tax. The detailed guide describes a per-pan ticket; the main page says per person. Confirm your party’s ticket needs at the desk. General site admission is free.

Tuesday–Saturday, weather permitting. The detailed guide describes March–November outdoor troughs and December–February visitor-center troughs, but an older April–October summary remains. Call before a winter visit. The Sunday pilot has ended.
tripFacts.locator: Gold Panning; Hours; older seasonal summary

tripFacts.text: Visitor center, accessible panning area and restrooms, shaded picnic area and trails. Underground tours are a separate guided activity.

beforeYouGo: Confirm the current session schedule, especially during winter.
Check weather closures before setting out.
Ask how many pan tickets your family needs, including children under eight.
destinations.locator: Published activity policy and visitor details; see field-level references

overview.text: Maine Geological Survey describes gold in bedrock, glacial sediments, and stream deposits, with much of the gold found coming from stream-bed placers. Its published stream list is a starting point for research, not proof of permission or a promise of gold.

places.title: Swift River and tributaries · Byron area
places.text: Maine Geological Survey lists reported gold occurrences in the Byron area, in Oxford and Franklin counties. Check current ownership, land-manager requirements, and the rules for your intended equipment.
places.locator: Gold Panning Streams table; page updated April 12, 2023

accessNotes.title: Hand tools and motorized equipment are different categories
accessNotes.text: Maine Geological Survey’s 2023 guidance distinguishes hand-tool panning from motorized recreational prospecting and requires landowner permission. Motorized work has additional seasonal, equipment and closed-water restrictions. Check the current rules with DEP or LUPC for the township you plan to visit.
accessNotes.locator: General Regulations; Organized Or Unorganized Township?

mines.title: Millbrook Mine
mines.text: Gold and silver are listed in this past-producer record. Its surviving descriptions give a much more tangible picture of the workings.

historyNotes.title: A shaft beside the brook
historyNotes.text: MGS records a 105-foot vertical shaft with a six-foot crosscut at that depth, along with old foundations and a dump. It also notes bedrock exposed in the brook. These are historical record descriptions, not a current condition survey.

historyNotes.title: Another name to search
historyNotes.text: The database lists West Sullivan Group as a synonym. Its bibliography points to Young’s 1962 Hancock County evaluation, pp. 97, 99 and 104; the 1958 metal-mines index, pp. 28 and 49; and Morrill and Hinckley’s 1959 Eastern Maine volume, pp. 46 and 73.

MGS bibliography: pp. 28, 49; original pages await inspection

mines.researchNote: The named operating company and operating dates remain unresolved. No verified mine-specific photograph has been located.

mines.title: Golden Circle Mine
mines.text: An island gold-and-silver working with contemporary newspaper reports as well as a later state mineral record. Its history includes a proposed mainland stamp mill.
mines.dates: Activity reported in July 1880 and February 1881; full operating span unresolved.

location.description: Sorrento, Hancock County; MGS comments associate the working with Treasure Island.

historyNotes.title: March 27, 1880 · company certificate
historyNotes.text: Maine’s corporate register lists Golden Circle Mining and Milling Company, Sullivan, with a certificate filing date of March 27, 1880. This dates a company record, rather than the first excavation or present-day ownership.
historyNotes.locator: Printed p. 85 (PDF p. 87); general-law section definition

historyNotes.title: July 1880 · a shallow shaft
historyNotes.text: An Ellsworth correspondent reported the Golden Circle shaft at roughly 30 feet, with quartz said to contain gold. This is a contemporary report of work and claimed mineralization, not an independently established gold yield.
historyNotes.locator: Printed p. 72, Maine Mining News; correspondence dated July 26

historyNotes.title: February 1881 · a mill proposed
historyNotes.text: A later report said the directors planned a stamp mill in Portland because island accommodation was inadequate. It supports the proposal, but does not establish that the mill was built or operated.
historyNotes.locator: Printed p. 93, Maine Mining News; correspondence dated February 1

historyNotes.title: Names and later observations
historyNotes.text: MGS lists Silver Isle Mine and Silver Isle Mining Mine among the synonyms, and describes a 35-foot, two-compartment shaft. Its comments record a Treasure Island visit on November 21, 1997: steep ground, snow and ice prevented the shaft from being located.

mines.text: Despite its name, the record lists gold. Classified as a prospect, not a producing mine.

This is not an established opening date or proof of production.

mines.title: Pittston gold-seeking working
mines.text: Smith inspected pegmatitic workings locally called the Pittston gold mine during his 1903 fieldwork. A quartz sample chosen with the owners’ advice returned no gold or silver. The account documents an unsuccessful gold search, not a confirmed producing gold mine.
mines.dates: Work and a mill preceded the 1903 visit; opening and closing dates unresolved.

location.description: Pittston, Kennebec County; about three miles east of the Kennebec River in the historical account.

historyNotes.title: The mill at Nehumkeag Pond
historyNotes.text: Smith reports a quartz mill about a mile from the working, on Nehumkeag Pond. A mill’s existence did not establish a profitable gold deposit.

furtherReading.locator: Original field account · printed/PDF p. 85

destinations.title: Coos Canyon Rock & Gift
destinations.text: Try the motions before heading into a river. The shop offers a free panning demonstration and supervised tub practice using purchased paydirt. Added gold in paydirt is a practice aid, not evidence of natural river yields.

tripFacts.text: Byron · Coos Canyon on the Swift River. Visitor contact: 207-364-4900.

tripFacts.text: Ask staff for a demonstration or supervised paydirt session. Tell the shop ahead if your group exceeds eight.

tripFacts.text: A pan and water tub are provided for supervised practice. Panning equipment can also be rented.
Demonstration advertised as free. Panning setup rental: $5 plus a $15 refundable deposit. Paydirt costs extra; ask for today’s price.

overview.text: Nevada’s state mining report provides a recent, dated view of industrial gold production. Those statewide totals describe commercial output; they do not predict what an individual prospector will find.

facts.label: Reported annual gold production
facts.definition: Statewide production reported by mine operators. Published in 2025; not a current-year forecast or recreational yield.
facts.locator: Printed p. 23, Production Highlights and Table 1; PDF p. 26

overview.text: New Hampshire has documented gold in bedrock veins and stream gravels. NHDES describes small quantities and a short-lived nineteenth-century mining rush around Lyman and Bath. The Ammonoosuc district is a useful place to begin geological reading; it is not a map of places where you have permission to prospect.

history.title: Lyman and Bath’s short-lived gold rush
history.text: NHDES dates the Lyman discovery that sparked a local rush to 1864. Mines near Bath supplied two mills, but the operations were short-lived. This is a regional history date, not a verified first discovery for the whole state.

places.title: Ammonoosuc gold district · historical reference
places.text: The official fact sheet identifies a district centered on Lyman, Monroe and Bath, with gold in quartz veins and associated sulfide minerals. A historic district name does not establish current ownership, permission or an expected yield.

accessNotes.title: Hand panning and larger equipment follow different rules
accessNotes.text: NHDES’s 2020 guidance calls for landowner permission, prohibits shoveling into streambeds or banks for hand panning, and describes permits for dredging or similar work. Check current NHDES requirements and the relevant land manager before choosing equipment.
accessNotes.locator: Fact sheet p. 2 · dated guidance, reconfirm before a trip

mines.title: Dodge Gold Mine
mines.text: Hoskins places Dodge Gold Mine on the old Hall farm in Lyman. Ross’s field study adds a later chapter: intermittent work and a cyanide mill, with the mine already abandoned when he visited in summer 1915. Its exact modern entrance remains unresolved.
mines.dates: Worked before 1903; abandoned by Ross’s summer-1915 visit. Exact opening and final closing dates unresolved.

location.description: Old Hall farm, Lyman; precise workings not reconciled.

mines.locator: Lyman Master Plan, printed page 10; NHDES GEO-1 historical summary

historyNotes.title: The Hall family connection
historyNotes.text: Hoskins identifies the site with the farm settled by Abram Hall and Sarah Floyd. He says Abram lived there until his death in 1855, and that Abram Jr. later remained on the home place. These are farm-family details, not evidence that either man operated the gold mine.
historyNotes.locator: Printed p. 102 (PDF p. 128), Abram Hall biography

historyNotes.title: 1903 · mining remembered
historyNotes.text: Hoskins describes earlier extensive work at Dodge, and a separate nearby Tunnel Mine then being worked. His monetary and ore-quality claims are not independently verified here and are not used as production statistics.

historyNotes.title: The landscape today
historyNotes.text: Ammonoosuc Conservation Trust identifies the former Dodge Mine within its account of the Godfrey Memorial Conservation Area and says forest has reclaimed the site. The account does not establish permission to prospect or supply a mine-entrance coordinate.

historyNotes.title: A historical map connection
historyNotes.text: The 1957 USGS statewide mineral map lists Dodge alongside Allen, Atwood and Lisbon in Grafton County locality group 49. The grouped symbol and 1:500,000 scale are too broad to identify a precise entrance.

historyNotes.title: Summer 1915 · already abandoned
historyNotes.text: Ross reports a cyanide mill erected after Hitchcock’s 1878 account and intermittent later work. On his summer-1915 visit, Dodge was abandoned. This establishes its condition at that visit, not the exact date it closed.

historyNotes.title: A closer geological map
historyNotes.text: Ross includes a district geological map and structural sections. They help place the workings in their geological setting; no modern entrance coordinate has been derived from them here.
historyNotes.locator: Fig. 2, printed p. 274 / PDF p. 8; Fig. 3, printed p. 300 / PDF p. 34

furtherReading.locator: Original field report · printed p. 292 / PDF p. 26; geological map at PDF p. 8
Original town history · printed pp. 15 and 102 / PDF pp. 21 and 128
Original mineral map · Grafton County group 49
Land-manager account · Godfrey Memorial section

mines.researchNote: Reconcile the Ross and Hitchcock maps with a modern parcel and workings survey before adding a marker. The report narrows the history to an abandoned site by 1915, but does not supply an exact closing date or current access permission.

mines.title: Diamond Ledge Mine — identity under review
mines.text: NHDES reports a small gold shipment to the mint from a Diamond Ledge Mine in Ossipee. Similar names also occur in mineral-locality indexes. A reliable match between this account and a mine coordinate has not yet been established.

location.description: Ossipee in the NHDES account; exact mine identity unresolved.

historyNotes.title: A map lead, not a resolved identity
historyNotes.text: The 1957 USGS map separately lists White Diamond gold mine as Carroll County locality 6, referring to Meyers (1941). That name is a lead to compare with the NHDES Diamond Ledge account; the two records have not been proven to describe the same working.
historyNotes.locator: USGS MR-6, Carroll County locality 6; NHDES GEO-1 historical summary

historyNotes.title: Another Diamond Ledge · Dublin
historyNotes.text: Allison’s Dublin history names a Diamond Ledge Gold Mine Company and connects it to Gold Mine Road there. That is a separate town and account, not evidence locating the Ossipee working.

furtherReading.locator: Original mineral map · Carroll County locality 6

mines.researchNote: Do not substitute a mountain summit or county-centre coordinate for a mine. A primary document must reconcile the name and town before the site is plotted.

mines.title: Tunnel Mine · below Dodge
mines.text: A separate tunnel intended to reach the Dodge veins at depth. Ross describes it as about 900 feet long and says it failed to reach its intended target. It is retained as a distinct historical working, without an invented entrance point.
mines.dates: Worked in Hoskins’s 1903 account; already abandoned in Ross’s 1914–1915 field study.

location.description: Lyman; hillside below Dodge Mine in the historical descriptions.

mines.locator: Hoskins printed p. 15 / PDF p. 21; Ross printed p. 292 / PDF p. 26

historyNotes.title: An unsuccessful crosscut
historyNotes.text: Ross explains that the tunnel was driven below Dodge to intersect one of its large veins. Smaller veins were encountered, but the intended intersection was not achieved. Reported assays are not converted into a production total.

furtherReading.locator: Original tunnel description · printed p. 292 / PDF p. 26
Earlier town-history account · printed p. 15 / PDF p. 21

mines.researchNote: Find a separate entrance plan and reconcile the two accounts before assigning coordinates or a full operating span. The tunnel is not an open visitor destination.

mines.title: Diamond Ledge company working · Dublin
mines.text: Allison describes brief work by the Diamond Ledge Gold Mine Company in Dublin and says it found no gold. He associates the enterprise with the name Gold Mine Road. This gold-seeking working is kept separate from the unresolved Ossipee account.
mines.dates: Before Allison’s 1952 history; individual operating dates not established.

location.description: Dublin, Cheshire County; Gold Mine Road association, exact working unresolved.

mines.locator: Printed p. 99 / PDF p. 121, Nathan Methley section

historyNotes.title: A road name, not a gold confirmation
historyNotes.text: The town history preserves the company name and its road-name legacy. It supplies no entrance coordinates, operating dates or successful gold yield.

mines.researchNote: Locate corporate filings and a dated mine plan. Do not merge Dublin, Ossipee and White Diamond records because their names resemble one another.

destinations.title: Twin River Campground · Wild Ammonoosuc River
destinations.text: A managed river visit in Bath. The operator sells panning day passes at its store for about a mile of campground-controlled frontage. Get the pass and ask staff to show the permitted stretch.

tripFacts.text: 4 Twin River Lane, Bath, NH 03740 · junction of Routes 302 and 112. Contact: 603-747-3640.
Day visitors purchase a prospecting pass at the campground store. Access covers the operator’s frontage, not the whole river.
tripFacts.locator: Gold Panning day passes; visitor registration

tripFacts.text: Start with a pan. NHDES’s 2020 guide excludes shoveling into the streambed or banks. The operator advertises sluicing passes, but confirm current state requirements before bringing a sluice. Dredging requires a state permit and the operator’s approval.
tripFacts.locator: Operator equipment and dredging conditions; GEO-1 p. 2

tripFacts.text: A paid day pass is required for day visitors; a current panning-pass price was not published on the reviewed activity page. Ask the store.
The operator lists May 1–October 15. Call for day-pass availability and early/late-season office hours.
tripFacts.locator: What dates are you open?; How late can I arrive?

tripFacts.text: Campsites, cabins, cottages, restrooms with showers and a prospecting-supply store. Ask which amenities a panning-only day pass includes.

beforeYouGo: Confirm the day-pass price, check-in hours and permitted frontage with the store.
Tell staff exactly what equipment you plan to use; owner permission does not replace state requirements.
Check river conditions before entering the water; a pass does not establish safe conditions.

overview.text: Vermont’s gold history includes quartz-vein workings and stream placers around Bridgewater and Plymouth. Historical geological accounts describe uneven deposits and unreliable profit claims. For a practical starting point, Vermont State Parks publishes a specific hand-panning opportunity at Camp Plymouth, with clear equipment limits.

history.title: Two kinds of deposits, two different histories
history.text: E. L. Perry’s 1929 account distinguishes quartz veins from placer deposits. It dates a Bridgewater vein discovery to 1851 and reports Plymouth placer activity by about 1855. These district dates are not presented as Vermont’s first gold discovery.

history.title: Old production claims need careful handling
history.text: The same account warns that Plymouth’s reported historical dollar totals are unreliable. They are not converted here into a statewide production total or a prediction of what a visitor can find today.

accessNotes.title: State-park hand tools and streambed limits
accessNotes.text: Vermont State Parks allows traditional hand panning with small hand tools. Its rules exclude sluices, rocker boxes and powered or moving equipment, and limit material removal to the streambed rather than banks. The same page says gold panning is not allowed in state wildlife management areas.

accessNotes.title: Private-land sluicing needs separate approval
accessNotes.text: The Rivers Program’s May 2023 guidance requires landowner permission for private-land panning and both owner permission and state approval for sluicing on private land. It states that suction dredges for mineral prospecting in streams are prohibited. Ask the Rivers Program about current requirements for your proposed activity.
accessNotes.locator: PDF p. 1; contact details on p. 2

mines.title: Rooks Mine / Fox Mine
mines.text: A quartz-vein gold working near Plymouth, also known as Fox Mine. MRDS records production in 1883–1887. Later accounts disagree about when Henry Fox acquired it: Beth R. Smith gives a late-1887 auction, while State Parks says 1889. Neither establishes uninterrupted commercial production through his death in 1919.
mines.dates: 1883–1887 production in MRDS; Fox purchase dated 1887 or 1889 in different accounts; later searching through 1919.

location.description: Plymouth, Windsor County; Reading Pond / Buffalo Brook area

mines.locator: MRDS DEP_ID 10081526; State Parks history; Perry 1929 excerpt, PDF pages 10–11

historyNotes.title: 1903 · a geologist visits
historyNotes.text: G. O. Smith visited the old Rooks workings near Tyson. He could not inspect the openings and found little encouraging material on the dumps. His report describes an ambitious operation with no apparent profit.

historyNotes.title: 1929 · the hillside workings
historyNotes.text: Perry describes a brook-level adit and mill ruins, with upper shaft workings about 170 feet higher. He identifies native gold but describes its distribution as too irregular and low-grade for profitable mining. These are historical observations, not present conditions.

historyNotes.title: Henry Fox · two purchase dates
historyNotes.text: Beth R. Smith recounts Fox’s lawsuit for unpaid salary and a sheriff’s sale at Ludlow, placing his ownership in late 1887. State Parks instead gives 1889. The deed or court record is still needed to reconcile them.
historyNotes.locator: Smith, article p. 13 / compilation PDF p. 6; State Parks, History

historyNotes.title: A diagram and a face from the past
historyNotes.text: Smith’s article reproduces a cross-section from the company’s 1884 annual report and a photograph captioned as Henry Fox at his house in 1908. These appear in the linked scan. The company illustration is promotional, not a surveyed modern mine plan.

historyNotes.title: Reading the old claims carefully
historyNotes.text: The article questions the reliability of advertised returns. Its newspaper and company figures remain attributed historical claims, rather than verified production totals or evidence of gold available today.

furtherReading.locator: Original article scan · diagram and Fox photo at PDF p. 5; auction story at p. 6
Original field report · printed/PDF pp. 87–88
Perry’s later description · PDF pp. 10–11
Current park history · separate from historical workings and ownership

mines.researchNote: Confirm the acquisition year from the court sale or deed, locate the full 1884 annual report, and reconcile the old workings with a modern survey. Historical photographs are linked for inspection; no photograph or promotional diagram has been republished as a current site view.

mines.title: Taggart vein / Bridgewater Gold Mines
mines.text: Worked intermittently around 1859 west of Bridgewater Center. Historical accounts describe mills and claimed gold returns, but a sampled ore assay reported no gold. The GIS commodity fields emphasize lead and copper. This is evidence of gold-seeking activity, with disputed gold results.
mines.dates: Intermittent work around 1859; full operating span unresolved.

location.description: Bridgewater, Windsor County; Dailey Hollow vicinity

mines.locator: DEP_ID 10081187; 1904 and Perry 1929 excerpts, PDF pages 7–11

historyNotes.title: 1859 onward · the Thompson farm vein
historyNotes.text: Smith places the Taggart vein on the old Thompson farm, one mile west of Bridgewater Center, with intermittent work beginning in 1859 and openings along a small stream gulch.

historyNotes.title: An assay that did not confirm the gold claims
historyNotes.text: A sample from quartz and galena beside an opening returned no gold in the Survey laboratory, despite earlier claimed returns. One sample does not prove every part of the vein is gold-free; it does explain why the gold results remain disputed.
historyNotes.locator: Printed/PDF p. 87; assay by Doctor Allen

historyNotes.title: Separate nearby projects
historyNotes.text: Perry also describes a distinct Dailey Hollow project with a road to a mill at Chatauguay. Nearby mills and claims should not automatically be merged into Taggart’s history.

furtherReading.locator: Original description and assay · printed/PDF pp. 86–87
Compare the 1904 and 1929 excerpts · PDF pp. 7–11

mines.researchNote: A documented owner/operator chain, a reliable full operating span and a plan matching the various openings remain to be established. The historic MRDS point has unknown accuracy and is not a surveyed entrance.

destinations.title: Camp Plymouth · Buffalo Brook
destinations.text: A state-park hand-panning opportunity near Ludlow. The park explicitly allows visitors to pan in Buffalo Brook for personal enjoyment. Stay within the park’s permitted area; nearby historic mines are outside this invitation.

tripFacts.text: 2008 Scout Camp Road, Ludlow, VT 05149. Park contact: 802-228-2025.
Use the park’s day-use entrance and confirm the boundary and panning area with staff. Permission is for recreational hand panning in Buffalo Brook.
Hand panning only. State Parks permits small hand tools for streambed material; leave the banks intact. No sluices, rocker boxes or powered/moving equipment.
Standard day use: $5 ages 14+, $2 ages 4–13, free ages 0–3. Rates effective July 1, 2025; check the current fee page before travel.
Day use: Friday of Memorial Day weekend to the second September weekend, 10am–sunset. Cottages/group camping run later; that does not establish off-season brook access.
tripFacts.locator: Park Information: Season and Day Use Hours

tripFacts.text: Picnic areas, beach, boat rentals, group camping and cottages. Ask staff about the brook approach and any mobility needs.
tripFacts.locator: Park amenities; Group Camping; Cabins / Cottages

beforeYouGo: Check park alerts, day-use opening dates and current entry fees.
Ask staff to identify the park boundary and the permitted brook section.
Keep to hand panning; do not enter abandoned shafts or adits.

overview.text: Massachusetts is worth approaching with a geological map rather than a promise of a gold-bearing stream. USGS’s statewide surficial mapping distinguishes glacial till, meltwater deposits and younger river sediments. Those maps help explain the ground beneath a stream, but do not show that gold occurs there. No specific Massachusetts placer site has been verified in this first research pass.

history.title: Reported deposits are not the same as proven gold
history.text: Laurence La Forge’s 1932 Boston-area report records gold, copper and lead reports prompted by sulfide veins in quarries, but says valuable recoveries there were not established. This historical assessment concerns the Boston area; it does not prove that Massachusetts has no gold.

history.title: A useful map for reading the landscape
history.text: The statewide USGS compilation covers 189 quadrangles at 1:24,000 scale and distinguishes bedrock exposure, glacial deposits and postglacial sediments. Use it as a geology research aid, not a prospecting-access map.

accessNotes.title: Check the land manager before collecting
accessNotes.text: For DCR parks and forests, begin with DCR’s current Parks and Recreation rules and ask the park manager about your exact collecting activity. The agency separately lists draft rules under review; a draft or geological map does not establish permission. No public hand-panning site is verified here yet.

overview.text: Connecticut’s official mine inventory is a good starting point for researching historical mineral workings. Its technical report describes historical gold mining only as possible, while documenting many other commodities. This first pass has not verified a Connecticut placer-gold destination or a statewide gold-production figure. A mine symbol on a map should not be read as a gold find or visitor access.

history.title: A mining inventory, not a gold-mine count
history.text: The 2022 version 1.01 inventory documents 1,070 bedrock mining sites across many commodities, including mines and quarries of different activity statuses. That total is deliberately excluded from the gold statistics cards: it is not a count of gold mines.

accessNotes.title: State-land collecting is restricted
accessNotes.text: Connecticut DEEP says collecting rocks and minerals on state land is not allowed without authorization. Scientific or educational collecting may be considered through written application. Its mining database also warns that many listed sites are private property and that a mapped site grants no visiting permission.
accessNotes.locator: Rock and Mineral Collecting; database access qualification

overview.text: Rhode Island has historical prospects and small mines named for gold in USGS’s 1971 bedrock-geology report. The author emphasizes how little was known about when some deposits were worked, the extent of mining or even the commodity sought. Treat these as historical research leads, not established modern panning destinations.

history.title: What an old gold-mine name can tell us
history.text: Quinn’s report preserves names such as Durfee Hill, Snake Den and Bald Hill, while warning that mining records are sparse. The names alone do not provide reliable production totals, workable deposits or permission to collect.
history.locator: Printed p. 58 / PDF p. 66 · Metal Deposits

places.title: Durfee Hill · historical mine reference
places.text: Listed as a gold mine in the Chepachet quadrangle in the 1971 report. Present-day access and recoverable gold have not been verified here.

places.title: Snake Den and Bald Hill · historical references
places.text: The report lists Snake Den in the North Scituate quadrangle and Bald Hill in the East Greenwich quadrangle. These are old mine references, not directions to publicly accessible gold-bearing streams.

accessNotes.title: State camping access does not grant collecting rights
accessNotes.text: Rhode Island State Parks’ camping policies prohibit visitors from removing or disturbing rocks, fossils and minerals on state lands. A campground booking or nearby historic mine name is not collecting permission. No specific publicly approved panning destination has been verified in this first pass.

overview.text: New York’s rich mining history does not imply a comparable history of producing gold mines. The State Museum’s historical overview says colonial searches did not find gold and silver in economic quantities. No individual historic gold mine has been verified for this guide yet; that is a research gap, not proof that gold is absent.

Dahlonega anchors North Georgia’s gold-mining history. Georgia DNR describes a gold rush into the Cherokee Nation before the California rush. Today, a managed panning lesson offers a way to practice without treating historical mining districts as open-access sites.

history.title: Dahlonega’s mint and museum
history.text: The U.S. branch mint operated here from 1838 to 1861. The Gold Museum occupies the 1836 Lumpkin County Courthouse and interprets the region’s mining history; its museum listing is not a prospecting permit.

destinations.title: Consolidated Gold Mine · indoor panning practice
destinations.text: An instructor-assisted indoor panning experience in Dahlonega. A sample pan comes with paid underground-tour admission, or the operator offers a separate panning-only package. This is managed practice, not permission to work nearby streams.

tripFacts.text: 185 Consolidated Gold Mine Road, Dahlonega, GA 30533. Call 706-864-8473.
Choose a paid underground tour with its included sample pan, or ask about the separate panning-only option. The tour and panning area have different accessibility conditions.
Instructors help with the panning technique, and a souvenir bottle is provided. Ask which pan package suits your visit. Closed-toe shoes are recommended for the optional mine tour.
Published tour admission: $24.95 ages 13+ and $15.95 ages 3–12, plus tax, with a sample pan. Panning-only starts at $60. Confirm the package before purchase.
tripFacts.locator: Underground Tour pricing; separate panning price

tripFacts.text: Open daily 10am–5pm, rain or shine. Closed Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving and Christmas. Christmas Eve has shortened hours; check the operator’s current schedule.

Indoor panning and gift shop. Mobility devices are welcomed in the panning area, but the optional underground tour has stairs and excludes wheelchairs, walkers and strollers. Confirm your access needs directly.

beforeYouGo: Ask for the current panning-only package price if you do not want the mine tour.
Confirm accessible arrangements for the panning area separately from the underground tour.
Check holiday hours and group arrangements before traveling.
